blocks.text: Structural disorders result from abnormalities of, or damage to, the physical structure of the nervous system; examples are brain tumours and spinal cord injuries.

blocks.caption: Brain tumour: an abnormal growth or mass of cells in the brain
rows: benign (non-cancerous) or malignant (cancerous); may arise from glial cells or from neurons
exact cause unknown; risk factors include radiation exposure, family history and certain genetic mutations
depend on the location: headaches, severe nerve pain, paralysis, seizures, coma

blocks.prompt: Why do the symptoms of a brain tumour differ from patient to patient?
blocks.explanation: They depend on where the tumour is, because different parts of the brain control different functions.

items: Structural disorders: tumours, spinal cord injuries. Brain tumour: benign or malignant, from glia or neurons; treated by surgery, radiation, chemotherapy.
